1.explanation:
All of the Elixir grammar rules live inside the default export function in elixir.js. Within that function:

• The LOWERCASE_SIGIL (and similarly UPCASE_SIGIL) rule includes a sub-mode that begins and ends on `/…/`, which is intended only for things like `~r/.../`, but it will pick up the `/1` in a function capture if the preceding `&` or identifier makes it look like a sigil.

• The unnamed “regexp container mode” (the object whose variants begin with `/` and end with `/[a-z]*`) is designed to detect standalone regex literals, but it also triggers on the `/1` in `&letter?/1` because High-Light.js’s RE_STARTERS_RE matches the preceding context.

Together these two modes cause the slash in a function capture to be parsed as the start of a regex/sigil. To fix the bug, the grammar needs an explicit mode for function captures (something like `{ className: 'built_in', begin: /&${ELIXIR_IDENT_RE}\/\d+/ }`) or adjustments to the regex/sigil modes so they do not trigger on `&name?/arity`. This requires editing the default export function in src/languages/elixir.js where those modes are defined.
1.bug_scenario:
When highlighting this Elixir snippet:

    def has_letter?(str), do: str |> String.graphemes() |> Enum.any?(&letter?/1)
    def letter?(c), do: c =~ ~r/\p{L}/u

the built-in Elixir grammar treats the `/` in `&letter?/1` as the start of a regex or sigil delimiter. As a result everything from that slash up to the next slash is colored as a regex literal (red in the screenshot), instead of leaving the entire function-capture form `&letter?/1` un-highlighted (white) and continuing normal Elixir syntax highlighting.

2.explanation: In src/languages/elixir.js there is a custom “regexp container” mode whose variants include “begin: '/'” and “end: '/[a-z]*'” to detect Elixir regex literals. Because it simply looks for a leading slash after certain characters, it also captures the slash used in function captures (arity notation) like “&letter?/1”. That misclassification is the root of the broken highlighting, so the regexp container mode must be adjusted (or a new rule added) to avoid treating capture‐arity slashes as regex delimiters.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting an Elixir snippet that uses a function capture operator (e.g. &letter?/1), the highlighter treats the “/1” as the start of a regex literal and continues until it finds a closing “/”, mangling the rest of the line’s colors. In other words, the slash in the capture (arity) is mistaken for the regex delimiter.
